issues_detected.description: Only four keywords (voice, health, biomarkers, bridge2ai); none name the clinical conditions, modality (speech, cough, respiration), derived-feature types or PhysioNet, limiting searchability

issues_detected.description: The variables slot is absent entirely. issues_detected.description: collection_timeframes states data was collected over 12 months with no calendar dates, while distribution_dates spans six releases from November 2024 to May 2026 and version_access records growth from 306 to 833 participants, implying a longer collection window; the record flags the missing dates in source_caveats

issues_detected.description: Target enrollment is recorded as both 10,000 voices (project documentation) and 30,000 participants (IRB protocol and white paper) because the sources tie at the same rank; grant identifiers appear in four legitimate NIH surface forms plus two corrupted renderings quarantined in notes. semantic_insights: All DOIs use plausible registrar prefixes: 10.13026 (PhysioNet) for the v3.1.0, v3.0.0, v1.1 and pediatric datasets, 10.57764 (Health Data Nexus) for v1.0, 10.5281 (Zenodo) for the two archived code repositories; the version/concept DOI relationship is explained in version_access

All four recorded grant numbers (OT2OD032720, 1OT2OD032720-01, 3OT2OD032720-01S1, 3OT2OD032720-01S3) follow NIH application-type/activity-code/institute/serial patterns, and the two corrupted surface forms from the documentation are quarantined in notes rather than recorded as values
RRID:SCR_007345 in the citation is well-formed and is PhysioNet's resource RRID, appropriate for a PhysioNet citation

Human-subjects logic is fully satisfied: involves_human_subjects=true is matched by USF single IRB plus Canadian REB reviews, a partial HIPAA waiver for screening chart review, four consent modes with withdrawal rules, exact compensation amounts and a Certificate of Confidentiality

De-identification is appropriate to the data type: HIPAA Safe Harbor plus removal of indirect identifiers, narrative text, free-speech-derived spectral features and all raw audio, with the honest statements that k>=2 anonymity is not achieved and that voice is inherently identifying, matched by tiered access (registered features, controlled raw audio via Synapse and the DACO)

Version infrastructure is complete: six dated releases with per-version DOIs, a per-version changelog in errata and updates, semi-annual cadence with observed release dates cross-checked in source_caveats, and the note that v1.1 files are no longer available

Processing is reproducible: b2aiprep v3.0.0 named as the generator, with signal-processing parameters (mono 16 kHz Butterworth, STFT 25 ms window / 10 ms hop / 400-point FFT, 60 Mel bins, sparc at 50 Hz, torchaudio pitch 80-500 Hz, ppgs over 40 phoneme categories at 100 Hz) and a caveat that v1.1 used a 512-point FFT

related_datasets is a genuine typed graph: derives_from the controlled-access raw audio (Synapse syn72370534), is_supplemented_by the pediatric dataset (10.13026/h995-bt35), is_new_version_of three prior releases and is_version_of the concept DOI - keeping the pediatric release and the raw audio out of this dataset's own composition

Source disagreements (enrollment targets, hosting platform Health Data Nexus vs PhysioNet, grant identifier forms, PI affiliations, redacted contact emails) are recorded in source_caveats with the resolution rule that decided them rather than silently resolved

Temporal ordering is consistent: award start 2022-09-01, v1.0 end of November 2024, releases 2025-01-17 through 2026-05-01, award end 2026-11-30, and the v3.1.0 'no new participants' changelog agrees with the 833-participant count shared with v3.0

sub_elements.evidence: machine_annotation_tools.tools: Whisper Large, openSMILE, Praat, Parselmouth, torchaudio, sparc, ppgs, b2aiprep, senselab with per-tool descriptions; external_resources give repository URLs and licenses (b2aiprep Apache-2.0, redcap/docs MIT); b2aiprep pinned at v3.0.0 for this release
sub_elements.quality_note: software_and_tools slot unused, but tools are named with roles, repositories, licenses and (for the generator) a version; other tools lack versions.

sub_elements.evidence: conforms_to: BIDS v1.9.0; conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema; ICD-10 labeling; external_resources: Interspeech 2024 protocol paper, REDCap dictionary archived on Zenodo, docs site archived on Zenodo, FHIR profiles

elements.name: Dataset Evaluation and Limitations Disclosure
elements.description: Does the metadata communicate known risks, biases, or dataset limitations?

sub_elements.name: Known Limitations Documented
sub_elements.evidence: known_limitations: six typed entries - English-only coverage, five-site representativeness, temporal diagnostic drift, raw-audio/feature withholding scope, excluded multimodal data, methodological quality (AI-readiness data-quality criterion not met)
sub_elements.quality_note: Typed, specific, and cross-referenced to the consortium's own AI-readiness self-assessment in notes.

sub_elements.name: Biases Categorized Using Standard Taxonomy
sub_elements.evidence: known_biases: selection_bias, sampling_bias, representation_bias, measurement_bias and annotation_bias with descriptions, mitigation strategies for two and affected_subsets for two; future_use_impacts warns on distributional skews
sub_elements.quality_note: Five BiasTypeEnum categories including annotation bias from single-labeler diagnosis; no AIO mappings.

sub_elements.name: Data Anomalies and Quality Issues Noted
sub_elements.evidence: anomalies: site configuration and protocol changes, microphone distance and noise, diagnostic-practice variation, self-report inaccuracy, unaudited ML-derived text, feature-generation failures
sub_elements.quality_note: Concrete anomalies covering hardware, protocol, labeling and derivation.

sub_elements.name: Sensitive Content and Warnings Provided
sub_elements.evidence: sensitive_elements: race/ethnicity, sexual orientation, socioeconomic and mental-health information, biometric voice data; content_warnings: possible offensive or distressing content in free-speech tasks, with a caveat that transcripts and free-speech spectral features were removed from the release
sub_elements.quality_note: Sensitive categories are explicit and the residual exposure after redaction is quantified honestly.

sub_elements.name: Ethical Review Details Including Conflicts
sub_elements.evidence: ethical_reviews: USF single IRB (not drug/device, no DMC) and Canadian REBs with the separate genomic protocol noted; data_protection_impacts records the ethicist review and controlled-access memorandum
sub_elements.quality_note: Review bodies and process detailed; no explicit investigator conflict-of-interest statement.

sub_elements.name: Related Datasets with Typed Relationships
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: distribution_formats lists Parquet/TSV/WAV with PhysioNet and Synapse access_urls; license_and_use_terms.data_use_permission: general_research_use; third_party_sharing.is_shared=true
sub_elements.evidence: related_datasets: derives_from (Synapse raw audio), is_supplemented_by (pediatric dataset doi:10.13026/h995-bt35, 300 participants, 23,533 recordings), is_new_version_of (v3.0.0, v1.1, v1.0 on Health Data Nexus), is_version_of (concept DOI)
sub_elements.quality_note: Six typed relationships covering derivation, supplementation and full version lineage - the strongest expression of this sub-element the schema offers.

strengths: Complete identifier and version infrastructure: version and concept PhysioNet DOIs, RRID, six dated releases with per-version DOIs, changelog, semi-annual cadence cross-checked against observed release dates

Ethics documentation is end-to-end: dual-country IRB/REB reviews, partial HIPAA waiver, four consent modes with withdrawal terms, exact compensation, Safe Harbor-plus de-identification and honest k<2 and voice re-identification statements matched by tiered access

Reproducible processing: b2aiprep v3.0.0 with full signal-processing parameters (16 kHz, STFT 25 ms/10 ms/400-point, 60 Mel bins, sparc 50 Hz, ppgs 40 phonemes at 100 Hz) and version-specific parameter caveats

related_datasets forms a genuine typed graph (derives_from raw audio, is_supplemented_by pediatric, is_new_version_of three releases, is_version_of concept DOI), keeping the pediatric release and raw audio out of this dataset's composition
Source disagreements (enrollment targets, hosting platform, grant identifier forms, affiliations, redacted emails) are recorded in source_caveats with the resolution rule that decided them
weaknesses: Only four generic keywords; conditions, modalities and feature types are absent from the searchable tags
No variables slot at all: column-level metadata is delegated entirely to prose-described JSON data dictionaries, and is_tabular is unset
at_risk_groups_included=false is unreconciled with cohorts that include dementia and serious psychiatric illness
The release's own collection window is undated (a bare '12 months') despite six dated releases and cohort growth from 306 to 833 participants
No demographic distributions or per-cohort participant counts despite naming age, sex, gender, ethnicity and socioeconomic status as identified dimensions
recommendations: Expand keywords to at least ten covering speech, cough, respiration, the four disorder categories, acoustic features and PhysioNet
Add typed variables entries for the cross-file identifiers and principal phenotype columns, or attach the JSON data dictionaries as typed resources, and set is_tabular
Reconcile the at-risk flag with cohort composition: either set it true with consent-capability screening as the protection, or state why these populations are not classed as at-risk
Date the v3.1.0 collection window in collection_timeframes or scope the 12-month figure to the release it describes
Add per-cohort counts and demographic distributions to subpopulations from the release dashboard or missingness tables
